paper_type_evidence.quote: We have observed the Class 0 protostellar source IRAS 16293 − 2422 A in the C 17 O and H 2 CS lines as well as the 1.3 mm dust continuum with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array

question.value: What are the substructures, kinematic structures, and gas-temperature distribution in the disk-forming region of the Class 0 protostellar source IRAS 16293-2422 Source A on a 10 au scale?

evidence.quote: In this study, we make use of the ALMA data observed at a high spatial resolution ( ∼ 0 ′′ . 1; 14 au) and have a close look at the disk/envelope structure of IRAS 16293–2422 Source A
This study used the ALMA data set ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00457.S.
as well as the 1.3 mm dust continuum with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array
We employed the Band 6 receiver to observe the spectral lines of C 17 O and H 2 CS (Table 1).
The distribution of the C 17 O ( J = 2–1) line is extended along the distribution of the continuum emission over 300 au in diameter (Figure 3a).
The 1.3 mm continuum image was prepared by averaging line-free channels, whose total frequency range was 0.3 GHz.
Forty-four antennas were used in the observations.
The baseline lengths of the antennas ranged from 21.0 to 3696.9 m.
the typical size of the synthesized beam was ∼ 0 ′′ . 1 for each image

The angular resolution of the image with a uniform weighting is (0 ′′ . 106 × 0 ′′ . 064) ( ∼ 14 au × 9 au), which is slightly better than that with the Briggs weighting (0 ′′ . 128 × 0 ′′ . 080; ∼ 18 au × 11 au).

key_parameters.value: Inner radius = 50 au (or r_CB = 50 au), outer radius = 300 au, P.A. = 50 deg, V_sys = 3.9 km/s, flared angle = 30 deg, intrinsic FWHM = 1 km/s, emissivity proportional to r^-1.5

evidence.loc: 4.3.1. Keplerian Model for the C 17 O Line
evidence.quote: Here, the inner and outer radii of the model are fixed to be 50 au and 300 au according to the observed molecular distribution.

The emissivity in the model is assumed to be proportional to r − 1 . 5 , where r denotes the distance from the center of gravity, and is to be zero for r < 50 au and r > 300 au. The scale height of the disk is assumed to increase as increasing the distance from the center of gravity with the flared angle of 30 ◦ .

findings_qualitative.value: The 1.3 mm dust continuum of IRAS 16293-2422 Source A resolves into 5 intensity peaks (A1, A1a, A2, A3, A4) within 100 au, where A1 and A2 match extrapolated cm-wavelength positions and A3, A4, and A1a are newly detected.

evidence.quote: The continuum emission of the binary component, Source A, reveals the substructure consisting of 5 intensity peaks within 100 au from the protostar.

The positions of two continuum peaks (A1 and A2) are consistent with those previously observed at cm wavelength, if their proper motions are considered. They also agree with the recent report on the 3 mm continuum emission. We also detect new continuum peaks (A3, A4, and A1a).

findings_qualitative.value: C17O (J=2-1) traces a rotating circummultiple structure on a 300 au scale centered at the continuum intensity centroid and is strongly depressed within a radius of 50 au.

evidence.quote: The C 17 O emission mainly traces the circummultiple structure on a 300 au scale centered at the intensity centroid of the continuum, while it is very weak within the radius of 50 au from the centroid.

findings_qualitative.value: H2CS lines trace a compact (r ~ 30 au) rotating circumstellar disk centered on continuum peak A1, which has a different rotation centroid, systemic velocity (2.5 km/s vs 3.9 km/s), and central mass than the circummultiple structure.

evidence.quote: The H 2 CS emission, in contrast, traces the rotating disk structure around one of the continuum peaks (A1). Thus, it seems that the rotation centroid of the circummultiple structure is slightly different from that of the disk around A1.

evidence.loc: 4.4.5. Comparison between the Circumstellar and Circummultiple Structures
evidence.quote: As well, the difference of the systemic velocity between the two models, 3.9 km s − 1 for the circummultiple structure and 2.5 km s − 1 for the circumstellar structure, implies a potential motion of the protostar A1 in Source A.

findings_qualitative.value: The H2CS rotation temperature steeply rises to >= 300 K at the 50 au transition zone between the circummultiple structure and the A1 circumstellar disk, suggesting a ring-like hot corino heated by accretion shocks and/or protostellar radiation on piled-up gas.

evidence.quote: As approaching to the protostar A1, the rotation temperature steeply rises up to 300 K or higher at the radius of 50 au from the protostar. It is likely due to a local accretion shock and/or the preferential protostellar heating of the transition zone from the circummultiple structure to the disk around A1.
‘Hot corino’ may have a ring-like structure, instead of a simple spherical or disk-like structure.

claims.hypothesis: IRAS 16293-2422 Source A is a multiple protostellar system with compact substructures within its disk/envelope system.
claims.experiment: Image the 1.3 mm dust continuum at ~0''.1 (14 au) resolution with Briggs (robust=0.5) and uniform weighting, fit peak positions with CASA viewer, and compare with extrapolated VLA cm continuum proper motions.
claims.result: Five continuum peaks (A1, A1a, A2, A3, A4) are identified within 100 au; A1 and A2 match extrapolated VLA positions while A3, A4, and A1a are newly identified at 1.3 mm.
claims.finding: IRAS 16293-2422 Source A is likely a multiple system embedded in a ~300 au circummultiple structure.

evidence.quote: The continuum emission of the binary component, Source A, reveals the substructure consisting of 5 intensity peaks within 100 au from the protostar.

The positions of two continuum peaks (A1 and A2) are consistent with those previously observed at cm wavelength, if their proper motions are considered. They also agree with the recent report on the 3 mm continuum emission. We also detect new continuum peaks (A3, A4, and A1a).

claims.hypothesis: The circummultiple structure of Source A and the circumstellar disk around protostar A1 have distinct kinematic centers, central masses, and systemic velocities.
claims.experiment: Construct PV diagrams of C17O (J=2-1) centered on the continuum intensity centroid and H2CS (7_4,3-6_4,2, 7_4,4-6_4,3) centered on peak A1, and fit 3D Keplerian and infalling-rotating envelope models via reduced chi-squared tests.
claims.result: C17O traces a 50-300 au structure centered at the continuum centroid (V_sys = 3.9 km/s, M = 1.5-2.5 M_sun Keplerian or 0.6-1.2 M_sun IRE), whereas H2CS traces a r <= 30 au Keplerian disk centered on A1 (V_sys = 2.5 km/s, M = 0.4-0.8 M_sun).
claims.finding: The rotation centroid, central mass, inclination angle, and systemic velocity of the circummultiple structure differ from those of the circumstellar disk around A1, indicating A1 is one component of a multiple system with a potentially tilted disk.

evidence.loc: 4.4.5. Comparison between the Circumstellar and Circummultiple Structures
evidence.quote: First, the central mass estimated for the circummultiple structure is from 1.5 M ⊙ to 2.5 M ⊙ with the Keplerian disk model and from 0.6 M ⊙ to 1.2 M ⊙ with the infalling-rotating envelope model. These values are larger than the central mass from 0.4 M ⊙ to 0.8 M ⊙ (the Keplerian model) and from 0.15 M ⊙ to 0.25 M ⊙ (the infalling-rotating envelope model) estimated for the circumstellar structure around A1.

evidence.loc: 4.4.5. Comparison between the Circumstellar and Circummultiple Structures
evidence.quote: Thus, the differences of the inclination angle and the systemic velocity imply that the rotating disk structure around A1 could be tilted with respect to the circummultiple structure of Source A.

claims.hypothesis: Gas temperature experiences a local steep rise at the transition zone (~50 au) between the circummultiple structure and the circumstellar disk around A1.
claims.experiment: Derive the H2CS rotation temperature distribution from the intensity ratio of the (7_4,3-6_4,2, 7_4,4-6_4,3) and (7_2,5-6_2,4) lines in integrated maps, velocity channel maps, and line-of-sight maximum maps (moments=[8]).
claims.result: The maximum intensity ratio and rotation temperature along the line of sight steeply increase at a radius of 50 au from A1 up to >= 300-400 K and flatten inward of 50 au.
claims.finding: A local temperature rise occurs in a ring-like transition zone at r ~ 50 au, likely due to accretion shocks and/or unshielded protostellar heating of vertically piled-up gas, giving the hot corino a ring-like structure.

why_this_method.value: H2CS K-structure lines have very slow radiative transitions between different K_a levels, making their rotation temperature a good measure of gas kinetic temperature; using the 7_2,5-6_2,4 and 7_4,3-6_4,2/7_4,4-6_4,3 pair avoids line blending affecting the 7_0,7-6_0,6 line, and taking the maximum along velocity channels disentangles envelope and disk components along the line of sight.

evidence.quote: These are contaminations of the (CH 3 ) 2 CO (18 5 , 13 –17 6 , 12 EE and 18 6 , 13 –17 5 , 12 EE at 224.700 GHz) transitions, the CH 2 DOH (7 2 , 6 –7 1 , 7 , e 1 at 224.701 GHz; 20 1 , 19 –20 0 , 20 , e 1 at 224.725 GHz) lines, and/or an unidentified line. evidence.quote: It should be noted that very high temperatures obtained at some positions would be artificial. Since the intensity ratio at these positions are close to the high-temperature limit (1.47 for T = ∞ ) as shown in Figure 13(b), the derived temperature is sensitive to a small change in the ratio and suffers from a large error.

referee_caveats_inferred: Table 1 is omitted from the manuscript PDF text, leaving exact rest frequencies, upper state energies, and individual line beam sizes unstated in the text.
The 3D kinematic models neglect radiative transfer and continuum optical depth in a source where 1.3 mm dust brightness temperature reaches ~70 K.

The maximum-along-line-of-sight (moment 8) ratio method is susceptible to positive noise bias in low-S/N channels, which can artificially inflate the derived H2CS rotation temperature near the 1.47 asymptotic limit.
